"""Offline experiment: multi_scale_transformer with increased capacity for PathMNIST 9-class."""
import torch
from lightning_components import build_network
from worker_runtime import fit_model, batched_logits


def build_model(context):
    parameters = context["parameters"]
    return build_network(
        "multi_scale_transformer",
        in_channels=3,
        n_classes=9,
        hidden=parameters.get("hidden", 128),
        depth=parameters.get("depth", 3),
        dropout=parameters.get("dropout", 0.1),
        scales=tuple(parameters.get("scales", [2, 4, 7])),
        num_heads=parameters.get("num_heads", 4),
        mlp_ratio=parameters.get("mlp_ratio", 4),
        pooling=parameters.get("pooling", "mean"),
    )


def train(context):
    return fit_model(context, build_model(context))


def predict(context):
    model = build_model(context)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(context["checkpoint"], map_location="cpu", weights_only=True))
    return batched_logits(model, context["data"]["images"], context["config"])

experiment.hypothesis: Increasing multi_scale_transformer capacity (hidden 64→128, depth 2→3) will improve discrimination of visually confusable histopathology classes (background/debris/mucus, smooth muscle/stroma, normal mucosa/adenocarcinoma) by providing more representational bandwidth in the joint-attention fusion of multi-granularity tokens, while the 196-token fine-scale branch remains regularized by cross-scale attention and dropout.

decision.rationale: The first trial (multi_scale_transformer, hidden=64, depth=2) achieved 99.05% val accuracy and early-stopped at epoch 11. The model is small relative to the ~90k training samples. Increasing hidden width to 128 and depth to 3 should provide more capacity to distinguish the confusable histopathology classes (background/debris/mucus, smooth muscle/stroma) without overfitting, since the 196-token fine-scale branch still has sufficient regularization from the joint attention mechanism. I keep the same scales [2,4,7], pooling='mean', and num_heads=4 to isolate the capacity effect. Training uses the same AdamW + cosine schedule that worked well, with slightly tighter early stopping (min_delta=0.003) to capture small improvements. 25 epochs gives ample room for the larger model to converge while staying well within the 1-hour timeout (~82s/epoch × 25 ≈ 34 min).
